meeting_header:
Date: 2026-05-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:53 UTC (53 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM) — Samantha Ortiz (Brightline VP Eng), Arjun Patel (Brightline Platform Lead), Lena Morris (Brightline SRE), Tom Gallagher (Brightline Security), Naomi Wu (Brightline Product)
summary: Follow-up bridgecall after Brightline escalated availability degradation last week. Goal: align on mitigations, validate redundancy gaps in Dedicated deployment plan, agree benchmark/test scope and pilot SLA, and handoff to pilot kickoff. Customer remains concerned about multi-region failover latencies and auditability of KMS keys. SE offered stress testing and proposed short-term configuration change to reduce single-GPU KV cache eviction during bursts.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this tight. quick agenda: recap, mitigation options, bench plan, next steps.
[00:00:15] Samantha Ortiz: thanks Maya. yeah from our side we had a pretty bad late-night surge last thursday, saw 6–8s token latencies for short prompt paths which blew our SLAs and triggered retries.
[00:00:33] Arjun Patel: and a couple of times our fallback to smaller model caused mismatch in outputs, so product got unhappy.
[00:00:42] Diego Ramirez: yeah hi all SE here, i've looked at traces — looks like the problem is two-fold: an uneven shard distribution plus an eviction pattern in the KV cache under a hot prefix mix. so effectively one GPU was getting thrashed, hitting mem pressure and parallel token slowdowns.
[00:01:05] Lena Morris: just to be clear are we talking about dedicated or hosted? we thought we were on Dedicated reserved pool with 3x A100s.
[00:01:14] Maya Chen: good question — Brightline is on Dedicated, but you were using burst capacity to a different region last week, right?
[00:01:22] Naomi Wu: yes we rerouted to eu-west as a quick mitigation because us-east had higher queuing. maybe that changed the shard placement.
[00:01:34] Diego Ramirez: exactly, cross-region burst can re-trigger placement heuristics that end up co-locating heavy shards. our mitigation is two parts: short term config (pinning shard affinity + KV-cache-size bump) and medium term deploy change (more even shard split and fallback routing policy).
[00:01:55] Tom Gallagher: security wise we also need to confirm that when you do pinning or rebalancing, key material never leaves our VPC/HSM boundary — we have to see audit trails.
[00:02:05] Maya Chen: totally — we will share the security artifact set. Redwood's Private + Dedicated integrations support customer-managed KMS; we'll produce the audit log extract format.
[00:02:16] Samantha Ortiz: ok, high level sounds doable, but we need numbers — like how much latency improvement from KV bump vs shard split.
[00:02:25] Diego Ramirez: understood. propose a two-stage benchmark: 1) a 2-hour synthetic stress run that mimics your hot-prefix distribution with current config; 2) an A/B test with the pinning+cache bump. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 and tail coupling.
[00:02:43] Arjun Patel: will that run with our real prompt mix? we have some really long multi-turn flows that amplify kv pressure.
[00:02:51] Diego Ramirez: yes please — best if you give us a 30–60 minute sample trace; SE will replay it in Dedicated staging. there may be slight transcription — sorry replay not transcription, replay.
[00:03:03] Lena Morris: (laughs) alright. also we need to confirm fallback behavior — last time fallback gave inconsistent model outputs, was that because of quantized variant mismatch?
[00:03:12] Diego Ramirez: good call. fallback routed to a lower capacity variant which uses 4-bit quantization; model outputs can differ. we can set a modal policy that prefers model-variant parity and fall back only to warm-canary replicas to preserve deterministic behavior.
[00:03:29] Samantha Ortiz: what about cost? pinning and keeping warm replicas mean more $$.
[00:03:34] Maya Chen: yes there's a cost/latency tradeoff — we can show a few pricing scenarios. for pilot we usually propose a time-boxed commitment with surge credits and a rollback window.
[00:03:46] Tom Gallagher: we also have one red flag — we need to validate SOC 2 artifacting for message retention and log integrity. can you provide the exact fields in the per-request audit?
[00:03:56] Priya Nair: we'll include the audit schema — timestamps, model variant ID, shard placement id, request token counts, and KMS envelope id. we'll also provide sampling options to avoid PII leakage.
[00:04:12] Naomi Wu: perfect — please add an example export.
[00:04:18] Diego Ramirez: quick note: when doing the cache bump there is a slight uptick in cold-start memory; we expect no more than 5–8% additional GPU memory. it avoided eviction storms in our internal repros.
[00:04:32] Samantha Ortiz: hmm okay. what about multi-region failover? our regulatory folks require sub-2s failover for EU customers. last time failover was 6s.
[00:04:43] Diego Ramirez: failover time is dominated by two things: route convergence and KV priming. we can implement fast route cutover plus a lightweight prefix priming step to bring hot keys into cache before switching traffic. that combination got us to ~1.8s in a prior customer test.
[00:05:02] Arjun Patel: can we see that test?
[00:05:05] Diego Ramirez: yes we'll replicate it.
[00:05:08] Maya Chen: moving to pilot scope: we propose a 4-week pilot: week 0 config + bench, week 1–2 controlled load tests and live canary at 10–25% traffic, week 3 readiness review and roll to full production. success criteria: p99 under 1.5x baseline, no SLA breaches during 72h high-load window, and audit acceptance by security.
[00:05:31] Lena Morris: that seems reasonable. our timeline is tight: procurement wants a signed pilot by next week if the security answers look good.
[00:05:40] Tom Gallagher: yes procurement will need the pilot doc and we need to sign NDAs.
[00:05:44] Maya Chen: note captured — Maya to send pilot doc + contract.
[00:05:48] Samantha Ortiz: one last technical ask: can you show which kernel optimizations are active for our model? earlier we saw some kernel not being used and performance was worse.
[00:05:58] Diego Ramirez: yes i'll include the kernel profile and compile flags. small caveat: some flags are heuristics that vary by sequence length. we'll annotate expected perf delta per sequence bucket.
[00:06:12] Naomi Wu: and logs — please show a sample of the audit log with KMS envelope ids masked.
[00:06:18] Priya Nair: will do.
[00:06:21] (00:06:21) short pause and background noise; someone typing
[00:06:37] Samantha Ortiz: ok let's go through a quick risks checklist. risk one: regression after pinning.
[00:06:44] Diego Ramirez: mitigations: run canary, observe baseline delta for 48h, quick rollback script. risk two: added cost — mitigations: surge credits and time-box pilot. risk three: compliance — mitigations: provide audit schema + KMS proof-of-concept in staging with your HSM.
[00:07:06] Tom Gallagher: we want to see the HSM integration plan.
[00:07:09] Diego Ramirez: i'll create a technical runbook showing steps and logs you'll get.
[00:07:16] Arjun Patel: also curious about autoscaling behavior — last incident correlated with scale events.
[00:07:21] Diego Ramirez: right, autoscaler reacts to queue depth and latency; during a rapid surge it can overshoot or underserve depending on scale cooldowns. we'll tune cooldowns in pilot and add a soft-limit guard to reduce oscillation.
[00:07:36] Samantha Ortiz: ok that seems thorough. anything else from Redwood?
[00:07:40] Maya Chen: just to confirm next steps — we'll run the stress benchmark, share security artifacts, and send pilot contract. anything else from Brightline?
[00:07:49] Naomi Wu: procurement needs the pricing tiers and rollback SLA.
[00:07:53] Maya Chen: noted.
[00:07:56] (crosstalk)
[00:08:02] Samantha Ortiz: can you also include a short cost model: pin vs no-pin vs warm replicas.
[00:08:08] Maya Chen: yes we'll include three scenarios with monthly delta.
[00:08:12] Diego Ramirez: action item reminder: i'll schedule bench and post results.
[00:08:16] Samantha Ortiz: thanks all.
[00:08:20] Maya Chen: quick recap and we'll wrap — Diego run bench, Maya send docs/contracts, Tom send compliance Qs; we reconvene after bench results.
[00:08:31] Naomi Wu: can we do follow-up on 2026-06-03 at same time?
[00:08:35] Maya Chen: yes tentatively scheduled.
[00:08:38] (meeting wraps, 00:53 total)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words and some speaker label drift; timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: Pilot proposal deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/pilot-proposal-bl.pdf), Security package (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-bundle.zip), Benchmark folder (link: https://redwood.ai/shared/benchmarks/CRM-BL-9421).
